key_insight: SearchOS-V1 aims to make open-domain search agents more reliable by helping them track progress and avoid getting stuck in repetitive search loops. The key idea is system-level collaboration that improves evidence gathering when web searches fail.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a common failure mode in information-seeking agents: as search histories grow, agents lose track of task progress, repeat unhelpful searches, waste budget, and produce incomplete or low-quality answers.
method: Introduces a multi-agent system designed to coordinate search behavior in open-domain information-seeking tasks.
Focuses on maintaining task progress awareness so agents can better decide when to continue, switch strategies, or stop searching.
Aims to reduce repetitive loops after unsuccessful search attempts and improve evidence collection efficiency.
impact: This matters for practitioners building search-enabled LLM systems because it can improve answer quality, reduce wasted tool calls, and make agent workflows more robust in long-horizon tasks. It is especially useful for applications where completeness and budget efficiency are critical.
visual_elements: A flow diagram showing a search loop and how SearchOS breaks repetitive cycles.
A side-by-side comparison of baseline agents versus SearchOS in search success and budget usage.
An agent collaboration schematic showing roles and coordination across multiple agents.
An icon-based progress tracker illustrating task state, evidence gathered, and remaining search budget.
paper_title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
paper_authors: Yuyao Zhang, Junjie Gao, Zhengxian Wu, Jiaming Fan, Jin Zhang
